privacySeoDescription: How {appName}, the agents you choose, and this website handle your information.
privacyIntro: This policy describes the current {appName} application and website. {appName} is an open source project operated by {operatorName}.
privacyLocalBody: The current version of {appName} runs on your device and stores the configuration and session data it manages locally. {appName} does not upload your code, conversations, or usage data to servers operated by {operatorName}.
privacyAgentsTitle: Agents and tools from other providers
privacyAgentsBody: {appName} starts the third-party coding agents you configure. These agents and their tools may send prompts, code, context, and other data to their service providers according to your configuration and actions. Their providers’ privacy policies and terms apply to that processing. Repository operations may also connect to the Git remotes you configure, including when checking remote status.
privacySharingBody: To coordinate work, task descriptions, reports, and relevant context pass between participating sessions. When this information enters another agent's session, it may be processed by that agent's configured provider. Working with agents from different providers may therefore involve sharing task information with multiple providers.
privacyWebsiteBody: This is a static website hosted on GitHub Pages. We use a cookie to remember the language selected or detected for this browser for one year. We do not add analytics or advertising trackers. GitHub records visitors' IP addresses for security purposes; see GitHub's privacy statement.
privacyContactTitle: Information you choose to send us
privacyContactBody: If you contact us by email or through GitHub Issues, we receive the information you choose to provide and use it to respond to your request. Information posted in a public issue is visible to others. For privacy questions, contact {operatorName} at the email address below.
privacyFutureBody: Remote host support is planned and is not an available feature. This policy does not describe it.

faqSetupQuestion: Do I need to set up my projects and CLI configuration again?
faqSetupAnswer: Add your existing project folder without moving your code. The default account uses your existing CLI configuration, and the agent still loads your project's instructions, skills, hooks, and MCP servers. Additional accounts use separate configurations, with optional sharing of supported settings.
faqDataQuestion: Where do my code, account details, and conversations go?
faqDataAnswer: {appName} stores its application data locally and doesn't upload your code or conversations to its own servers. Each agent manages its own credentials and conversation records. Agents and tools connect to their providers according to your configuration and may send prompts, code, and related context.
faqParallelQuestion: Can sessions working on the same project cause conflicts?
faqParallelAnswer: Sessions share the project directory by default, so simultaneous edits to the same files can conflict. For parallel tasks, you can ask agents to use separate Git worktrees and review the changes before merging.
faqPortabilityQuestion: Can I go back to working in the original CLI?
faqPortabilityAnswer: Yes. Your project files stay in their original folders, and each agent keeps its own conversation records. You can resume through the original CLI as long as that conversation is still available. For an additional account, point the CLI at that account’s configuration directory.
